corrected_value.authors: Leventhal AM, Stone MD, Andrabi N, et al
corrected_value.title: Association of e-cigarette vaping and progression to heavier patterns of cigarette smoking

decisions.location: Introduction (lines 26-27); Methods, Measures and Data analysis (lines 30, 38); Results (line 51); Discussion and Conclusion (lines 52, 54); References 22 (lines 312-322)
decisions.quote: The current replication study confirms that e-cigarette use by non-smoking adolescents is associated with increased odds of subsequent combustible tobacco smoking initiation; that more frequent e-cigarette use is associated with more frequent subsequent tobacco smoking; and that the ‘reverse’ association applies, namely that tobacco smoking among never users of e-cigarettes is associated with greater odds of later e-cigarette use. These findings are consistent with previous studies,21 22 30 31 employ various adjusted analyses and sensitivity analyses and extend the findings from the US to a European context.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. Although the paper refers collectively to 'the cornerstone study by Leventhal et al.21 22' because both original JAMA articles analyzed the same US adolescent cohort, it explicitly formulates and empirically retests distinct findings from both publications using new longitudinal survey data from the Netherlands and Flanders. Research Questions 1 and 3 retest smoking initiation among baseline never-smokers and reverse initiation from Leventhal et al. (2015, Ref 21, 10.1001/jama.2015.8950, represented by shipped row 141). Research Question 2 explicitly follows Leventhal et al. (2016, Ref 22, 10.1001/jama.2016.14649) to retest the dose-response association between four-level baseline e-cigarette vaping frequency and three-level follow-up cigarette smoking frequency using ordinal logistic mixed regression adjusting for time, school, and baseline smoking frequency, and compares the resulting positive frequency association directly to Ref 22 in the Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Because Ref 22 reports a distinct published empirical finding on progression to heavier smoking frequency that is not covered by the 2015 initiation paper in shipped row 141, target_index 1 is a genuinely missing original target.
